newsitem.title: USA: EU, U.S. share biotechnology information.
newsitem.headline: EU, U.S. share biotechnology information.

text.p: European Union and U.S. Agriculture Department officials finished two days of "informational" talks on Friday about genetically-modified products.
"The talks were for informational purposes to find out where we're both at today," said Tim Galvin, associate administrator of USDA's Foreign Agricultural Service.
"The next couple months are a rather critical period for the EU, which plans to issue its own draft regulations in two or three weeks," he added.
Environmentalist groups in Europe held a series of demonstrations last autumn against imports of genetically-modified corn and soybeans developed by U.S. companies.
In developing draft regulations, EU agriculture officials will address controversial food safety and environmental issues, as well as product labelling.

"The EU expressed a very strong desire for more information from U.S. companies going through the regulatory approval process here, in anticipation that they will face similar requests," Galvin said. "There's a strong interest in data exchange."
